newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian parliament panel backs balanced budget.
newsitem.headline: Latvian parliament panel backs balanced budget.

text.p: The Latvian parliament's key economics and finance committee on Tuesday backed the 1997 budget, which foresees no deficit, and asked for a special parliament session to pass the budget at its first reading.
The parliament press service said the panel wanted a session on Monday, October 7. Parliament usually meets on Thursdays.
"If the committee gives such a recommendation, the parliament leadership usually goes along with it," a parliament spokesman told Reuters.
The deficit-free budget is one of the key planks of Prime Minister Andris Shkele's economic policy.
It was also drawn up to fulfill International Monetary Fund (IMF) conditions for credits.
The deficit in 1996 is expected to be around 40 million lats after a huge 90 million lats deficit last year in the wake of a banking crisis.
Shkele is likely to present the budget in parliament himself as Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss is due to leave his post after being dismissed from his political party.
